name: Telemetry Mock Generator
blurb: realistic sensor time series with noise, drift and faults
intro: Makes a seeded sensor time series from an explicit model: base + daily cycle + linear drift + random-walk wander + white noise, clipped to the sensor's range and quantised to its resolution, with spikes, dropouts, a stuck-at run and an offset step injected. Presets use typical datasheet resolution and noise; blank fields take the preset's value.

inputs.label: Samples
inputs.help: Up to 20000. 1440 at 60 s is one day.

inputs.label: Stuck-at run
inputs.help: The sensor repeats one value this long; 0 for none.

inputs.label: Offset step at mid-series
inputs.help: A recalibration or swapped probe; 0 for none.

examples.title: A day of room temperature at 1/min with faults
A week of battery drain every 10 min, as NDJSON

usage: Give sensor (a preset), interval in seconds, count of samples, start as an ISO UTC time, and optionally base, amp, period (h), drift (per hour), wander (σ per √h), noise (σ) and quant (resolution) in the sensor's unit (blank = preset); faults as spikes and dropouts in % of samples, stuck (samples) and step (offset); seed; format csv, json, ndjson or influx. Returns the data as a text output, summary statistics, a fault log and a chart. Use it for dashboard, parser and alerting test fixtures.
sources: Signal model: rule of thumb (deterministic cycle + drift + random walk + white noise, as in sensor error models, e.g. IEEE Std 952 for inertial sensors)
Preset resolution and noise from datasheets: Maxim DS18B20, Sensirion SHT31 and SCD30, Bosch BMP280, a 12-bit ±8 g accelerometer
mulberry32 PRNG (T. Ettinger) and the Box-Muller transform
